```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidymodels)
library(doParallel)
library(outliers) # grubbs.test
library(stringr) # string processing
library(isotree) # Outlier detection via isolation forest
library(gmodels) # CrossTable()

# tidymodels helper package
library(embed)
library(kknn)
library(discrim)
library(baguette)
library(rules)
library(earth)

tidymodels_prefer()
```

```{r}
combined_augmented_data = read.csv("combined_augmented_data.csv")
combined_augmented_data = combined_augmented_data %>% select(-cAb13)
# Retain variant value, replace replicate value with a rowname column to identify
# each sample. Color the final heatmap by the variant value and store prediction history
# alongisde rowname
fluorescence_sums = rowSums(combined_augmented_data %>% select(starts_with('cAb')))
avg_fluorescence = rowMeans(combined_augmented_data %>% select(starts_with('cAb')))

combined_augmented_data$batch = factor(c(rep(1, 288), rep(2, 456)))

labeled_augmented_data = combined_augmented_data %>% select(-Replicate) %>% 
  mutate("SampleNum" = row.names(combined_augmented_data), .before = Conc.) %>% 
  filter(Conc. > 0.1)

labeled_augmented_data
```

```{r}
# Attempting to train a model to predict from which batch a sample was drawn from
set.seed(0703)
batch_initial_split = initial_split(labeled_augmented_data, strata = batch) 
batch_training_data = training(batch_initial_split)
batch_testing_data = testing(batch_initial_split)
batch_folds = vfold_cv(batch_training_data, v = 5, repeats = 3, strata = batch)

batch_training_data %>% count(batch)
batch_testing_data %>% count(batch)
```
```{r}
# I'm trying to decide if this model should know the concentration. I'll include it in one
# but note that I did not convert it to a factor (still a dbl)
# RESOLUTION: With or without conc the CV results are very similar, they even
# use the same hyperparameters
set.seed(0703)
batch_recipe = recipe(batch~., data = batch_training_data) %>% 
  update_role(Conc., SampleNum, new_role = 'id')

batch_recipe_concentration = recipe(batch~., data = batch_training_data) %>% 
  update_role(SampleNum, new_role = 'id')

rf_batch_model = rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 1000) %>% 
  set_engine('ranger') %>% 
  set_mode('classification')

# I think the parameter set has to be different between both recipes? Because I need to 
# give it a potential mtry
rf_batch_params = rf_batch_model %>% extract_parameter_set_dials() %>% 
  finalize(x = batch_training_data %>% select(-c(batch, SampleNum)))
rf_batch_param_grid = grid_latin_hypercube(rf_batch_params,
                                           size = 30)

rf_batch_resample_results = rf_batch_model %>% 
  tune_grid(
    batch_recipe,
    resamples = batch_folds,
    grid = rf_batch_param_grid,
    control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE)
  )

best_rf_batch_params = select_best(rf_batch_resample_results)

rf_batch_conc_resample_results = rf_batch_model %>% 
  tune_grid(
    batch_recipe_concentration,
    resamples = batch_folds,
    grid = rf_batch_param_grid,
    control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE)
  )

best_rf_conc_batch_params = select_best(rf_batch_conc_resample_results)


collect_metrics(rf_batch_resample_results) %>% filter(.metric == 'accuracy') %>% arrange(-mean)
collect_metrics(rf_batch_conc_resample_results) %>%  filter(.metric == 'accuracy') %>% arrange(-mean)
best_rf_batch_params
best_rf_conc_batch_params

# Hyperparameters are the same for both models, with and wihout concentration
final_batch_rf_mod = finalize_model(rf_batch_model, best_rf_batch_params)
final_batch_rf_wf = workflow() %>% 
  add_model(final_batch_rf_mod) %>% 
  add_recipe(batch_recipe)

batch_rf_test = final_batch_rf_wf %>% 
  last_fit(batch_initial_split)
collect_metrics(batch_rf_test)
batch_rf_test$.predictions
```
```{r}
# Now lets try the same thing with a radial svm
set.seed(0703)

svm_batch_recipe = batch_recipe %>% 
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

svm_batch_model = svm_rbf(cost = tune(), rbf_sigma = tune()) %>% 
  set_engine('kernlab') %>% 
  set_mode('classification')

svm_param = svm_batch_model %>% extract_parameter_set_dials()
svm_batch_param_grid = grid_latin_hypercube(svm_param,
                                           size = 30)
svm_batch_resample_results = svm_batch_model %>% 
  tune_grid(
    svm_batch_recipe,
    resamples = batch_folds,
    grid = svm_batch_param_grid,
    control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE)
  )
collect_metrics(svm_batch_resample_results) %>% filter(.metric == 'accuracy') %>% arrange(-mean)

best_svm_conc_batch_params = select_best(svm_batch_resample_results)
final_batch_svm_mod = finalize_model(svm_batch_model, best_svm_conc_batch_params)
final_batch_svm_wf = workflow() %>% 
  add_model(final_batch_svm_mod) %>% 
  add_recipe(svm_batch_recipe)

batch_svm_test = final_batch_svm_wf %>% 
  last_fit(batch_initial_split)
collect_metrics(batch_svm_test)


# Ok so the radial svm provides much better performance on the test set than the random forest, so there may be something to using it as a feature to help predict variant
# Actually applying that to a random forest, however, doesn't yield better results, I actually think it harms the model
```
